_comment: Reachable ONLY via the portal contract (data/portals.json's new 'invrisil' row, requires_accomplishment invrisil_attuned, banked by the Guild-board letter beat)

floor_layers._pick: The marble plaza patch around the fountain -- OWNED wang tileset, pure-marble tile. CONTROLLER FIX 2026-07-08: [3,3] (row-major by wang id, id15 = pure marble), not the handoff doc's wrong [0,3] (a transition tile -- the doc's id->position table was corrected on main).

FIX WAVE facade assembly, handoff.md's recipe executed DATA-SIDE (per-cell picks; a committed composite of licensed pieces is forbidden in the public repo, and floor_layers rects accept negative y -- verified in tile_board_builder.resolve_layer_cells, plain range(), no grid clamp -- so the above-grid loom rows need no code). Layer 1/5: the cornice/roofline cap, Wall_Tiles (8,2) cool blue-grey stone (picks.md sec.2, MOCKUP-PROVEN), one row above the visible plaster at y=-2.

Layer 2/5: cream plaster upper floors, Building_Walls (26,2) (picks.md sec.1, MOCKUP-PROVEN flat #ddccb8) -- y=-1 (above-grid loom row) + y=0 (in-grid blocked row, cover_skip'd). Two plaster rows over a glass row = the 2-cell-facade scale-shock read, plus the cornice above.

Layer 3/5: the leaded-glass storefront line, Building_Walls (13,35) (picks.md sec.1, MOCKUP-PROVEN, 'USE SPARINGLY -- one shopfront band') -- exactly one band, the ground-floor row y=1 the player walks past.

Layer 4/5: pilaster strips every 3 cells (the spec's 'vertical LINES'), Wall_Tiles (8,2) stone columns spanning y=-1..1. Full 16px cells, not the mockup's 6px strips -- the cell-pick machinery has no sub-cell crop, so each pilaster is a full stone column dividing the glass line into 2-cell shopfronts (an honest approximation the windowed re-take judges).

Layer 5/5: the south band (y 16-17) -- building BACKS/rooftops seen from the street's north side, textured masonry variant Wall_Tiles (8,17) (picks.md sec.2's darker band) instead of the flat cool slab the windowed read flagged. Roofline texture, not facade (their fronts face away).

entities._comment: THE INVRISIL RETURN CARRIER, and the boulevard cluster's only way out. portal_menu_when SHIPPED WITHOUT its `requires` wrapper -- _door_gate_met reads .requires, so a bare {door_awakened:1} was an empty dict: vacuously true, the picker open from a fresh game. Wrapping it at door_awakened would have STRANDED the cohort that buys Eloise's 18g stone without ever awakening the Door, so the gate is door_mounted: the CARRIER-VS-ROW rule (test_portals' own audit) says a carrier may gate only on door_mounted or its own map's portals row counter, never tighter. Never author a *_when without the wrapper (data_lint's vacuous-gate arm).
entities.toast: A plain grey stone, out of place against the marble -- until you notice the coin-gold vein running through it, and the frame of light waiting just under the surface.
entities.observe: The Liscor stones were rougher. This one has been handled by people with better manners; it barely shows the wear.

entities.skill_hint_toast: The rooftops run straighter than the streets. Somebody up there knows it.
entities.locked_toast: Slate roofs and chimney smoke. The city keeps its second story to itself.

on_skill_use.toast: [Eagle Eyes] — The rooftop line resolves into a second city: runners' shortcuts, a watcher over Coyle's block, and two gentlemen who are always politely elsewhere.

entities._comment: Landing (1,7) on the alleys side sits inside that map's own west corridor, open + off every blocked/entity cell there.

entities.observe: Coin-gold trim on a merchant's collar, rings enough to case a fist. He totals you before you've said a word — cheaply, by the look on his face.
entities.friendly_line: He offers a smile with the price tag still visible on the underside. "Charming," he allows, in the tone of a man crossing an item off a ledger.
talk_pool: New face. I do like a new face — they're cheap, and occasionally they appreciate into something useful.
Everything has a price. The trick, which so few of you learn, is finding out whose.
Do step out of the doorway. You're blocking a view I paid a great deal to own.

talk_pool_stages._comment: b7 #207 ack (lowest priority — the #220 extorted/exposed pair keeps outranking per its order ruling).
lines: The letter arrived. Its contents priced three conversations I'd been having at a guess. You were paid four gold; it was worth forty. I will not be correcting the ledger.

talk_pool_stages._comment: b5 #220: pool-day texture for the bought-and-oily register the shipped hub variant set ('your retainer is current'). Ordered before exposed; exposure outranks if both ever bank.
lines: Prices hold for you. We have an arrangement, after all.
My consultant returns. Everything remains... current. Do spend some of it here.

talk_pool_stages._comment: b5 #220: pool-day texture matching the shipped wreckage facts (Guild took the charter, criers took the rest). Last slot outranks while banked.
lines: Enjoy the view. The criers certainly did.
The Guild holds my charter now. You hold my attention. Neither of us profits.

dialogue.text: A woman in a rose-dyed cloak checks a folded slip of paper against a shopfront number, unimpressed by both.
Blue-grey wool, city cut. She doesn't look at you. Nobody here looks at anybody.
A porter's barrow, half-unloaded, and a man in no hurry to finish the other half.
Olive work clothes, ink-stained cuffs. A clerk between one ledger and the next.
Mustard-brown coat, city boots, the specific walk of a man pretending he isn't lost.
Plum silk, a little too fine for the errand she's running. She counts her change twice.
A Gnoll traveler, tan road-cloak, watching the crowd the way a stranger watches weather.

entities.observe: Stacked shipping crates, waist-high, the kind of cover a man leans on to watch a street without looking like he's watching it.
entities.toast: You circle the block twice before it clicks: the modest COYLE AND SONS sign out front doesn't match the two wagons idling round the side, or the men counting crates like men who've been shorted before. Whatever Coyle's really running out of, the front door is the least of it.

entities._comment: GH#68 (Invrisil quest-stage rework): the FIGHT path's Stage 2 tailing chain, first leg.
entities.observe: A runner ducks out Coyle's side door with a ledger under one arm, moving with the particular haste of someone who'd rather not be noticed leaving.
entities.toast: You fall in a comfortable distance behind. The runner doesn't loop, doesn't double back -- just walks like a man with somewhere specific to be, heading for the alleys off the boulevard's east end.

entities.observe: Two shapes peel off the shadowed colonnade, unhurried, the way people move when they've done this before. Only after dark.
entities.gate_closed_toast: Nothing under the colonnade but shadow. Whoever works this corner keeps night hours only.

visual_states._comment: Marker visible ONLY while the night encounter_when gate can fire

entities.observe: Two heavy shapes lope along the lantern-line, wings folded tight, drawn to the light the way moths are. Only after dark.
entities.gate_closed_toast: The lantern-line is quiet. Whatever comes for the light only comes at night.

entities.observe: A chalked ring on the cobbles, two of Coyle's regulars leaning against the wall beside it, already sizing you up.
Panes racked like coins on edge. The glazier watches the street through his own stock, which is either pride or advertising.
Boots on pegs, sorted by wear. The pair in the window has walked to Pallass and back, if the sign is honest. Signs here mostly are.
Three tables, steam on the glass, and a chalk line of prices that assumes you already know what smoke-leaf costs in Invrisil.
